correctness.rationale: Each Y_n for n>=5 is cubic and triangle-free. With three initially blue vertices, any first force must center at a blue three-vertex path; the two possible rail-rail or rail-rung local shapes stall after the force, proving Z>=4. Two adjacent complete rungs force around both rails, so Z=4. For a size-four zero forcing set choose an actual first force. A fourth initially blue vertex permitting continuation must lie at one of four local neighboring positions for each of the two first-force shapes; these cases reduce to four disjoint families: adjacent full rungs (n); full rung plus two same-rail offsets (8n); full rung plus opposite-rail adjacent neighbors (2n); four consecutive same-rail vertices (2n). Constructive forcing sequences establish sufficiency and no wraparound identifications for n>=5; total exactly 13n. An entirely independent direct color-change enumerator compared all size <=4 subsets and families on n=5..11 (65,78,91,104,117,130,143), with no mismatches.
residual_risks: Only n>=5 stable prisms; n=3,4 excluded and have different basis profiles.
All-n proof uses the first-force local case split, not extrapolation from finite n<=11.
